items.t: Woman with 28 prior felony convictions arrested in Okeechobee drug investigation
items.x: An Okeechobee woman faces meth trafficking and other charges after deputies and DEA agents said they found 71 grams of meth, ammunition, pills and marijuana.

items.t: Briny Breezes residents call current flooding the worst they’ve seen
items.x: Residents in Briny Breezes are dealing with severe flooding from king tides, which are expected to continue through the end of October, prompting officials to urge caution.

items.t: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
items.x: The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey for what it calls disclosing classified information, employing the unusual maneuver of bypassing a grand jury.

items.t: Australian judge rejects prisoner’s claim that access to Vegemite spread is a human right
items.x: A prisoner has lost his challenge to an Australian state’s ban on inmates eating Vegemite after he argued in court that withholding the polarizing yeast-based spread breached his human right to “enjoy his culture as an Australian.”

items.x: WPTV has been following flooding on the Treasure Coast created by strong winds and king tides on Monday.

items.t: Seminole Ridge flag football eyes third straight state title
items.x: Over the past two years, the girls' flag football team at Seminole Ridge High School has won 37 games and lost only four, while winning two straight championships.

items.t: 'Have no word': St. Lucie County mourns firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge after on-duty death
items.x: Firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, who served St. Lucie County for over nine years, died Saturday while on duty, leaving his community grieving the loss of a second firefighter in his family within a year.

items.t: Trump says US is 'making a fortune' from higher oil prices. Who benefits?
items.x: President Donald Trump says higher oil prices are making America wealthier. But economists say the gains are concentrated among producers and investors, while consumers face rising costs.

items.t: 'Crash ur row only': United flight turned around after passenger allegedly said he'd 'hijack' plane
items.x: A United Airlines flight was diverted back to Las Vegas shortly after takeoff over the weekend due to what police said was a report of a passenger making a terroristic threat.

items.t: Construction complete: A closer look Palm Beach County's newest Boys and Girls Club
items.x: The club at Dreher Park will serve about 800 kids annually and features a Workforce Readiness Teen Center.

items.t: Hulk Hogan’s Florida mansion sells after price slashed by millions

items.t: Border crossing reopens with tighter checks for flesh-eating screwworm
items.x: Mexican cattle began moving on Monday through a border crossing as both Mexico and the U.S. work to stop the flesh-eating New World screwworm from spreading.

items.t: Justice Department files new charges against former FBI Director James Comey
items.x: The Justice Department has filed two criminal charges against former FBI Director James Comey, accusing him of unlawfully disclosing national defense information.

items.x: Congressman Jared Moskowitz is campaigning in Florida’s newly redrawn 25th District, addressing affordability, immigration enforcement, and his bipartisan record as he seeks reelection.

items.x: Former Boca Raton Mayor Scott Singer is running against Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz in Florida’s newly redrawn District 25, focusing on affordability, immigration, and accountability.

items.x: A proposal that could provide property-tax relief to Florida homeowners is raising concerns among Palm Beach County nonprofit leaders who worry the savings could come with consequences.

items.x: Some Palm Beach County residents have reported problems with touch voting machines and ballot options during early voting, prompting responses from election officials and party leaders.

items.x: Allegations of voting machines changing votes are circulating online ahead of the midterms, but experts and manufacturers say such issues are rare and often due to user error or screen calibration.
